search_lead.cognate: Armenian անուն (anown) and Greek ὄνομα continue *h1nomn; թողաք and καταλιπεῖν supply the same leave-behind predicate without an asserted etymological equation.
search_lead.argument: Armenian զքաջ անուն ... թողաք describes leaving the lineage’s good/heroic name to the church; Nicias wants to leave a reputation to future time, and failed invaders leave a name for their opponents. Thus name is enduring reputation, not a personal label, and it is the object of leaving. Useful external comparison, but Christian adaptation and ordinary reputation language remain serious alternatives to inheritance; no paired slab anchor for this precise wording.

search_lead.cognate: Armenian ոտիւք (otn, instrumental plural) / Greek πόδας (*ped-), Armenian ձեռաւք (jer̄n, instrumental plural) / Greek χεῖρας (*ghes-). Armenian կապեալ and Greek binding verbs are not asserted cognate.
search_lead.argument: The Armenian prisoner is bound at feet and hands, with repeated participle; Homeric Melanthius is bound hand and foot as a captive. Sirens passages repeat the paired-limb binding construction in voluntary restraint. Both body-part nouns are cognate, but ordinary restraint practice and possible Christian phraseology make inheritance uncertain. The slab Homeric partner Od. 12.442 lacks the binding verb, so this fuller parallel belongs to external review.
